title: Heat exchanger data sheets: five inputs that matter
summary: A practical guide to the process, thermal, mechanical and maintenance data needed for an industrial heat exchanger inquiry.
body:
A useful industrial heat exchanger inquiry needs enough process information to evaluate heat duty, equipment arrangement, materials and mechanical design. A drawing or a single flow rate is rarely sufficient for a reliable selection.

1. Flow rate and required thermal duty

Provide the flow rate on both sides, where applicable, and identify the required heating, cooling, condensation or evaporation duty. State whether the flow is continuous, intermittent or batch-based, and note any expected turndown or operating cases.

2. Inlet and outlet conditions

List inlet and target outlet temperatures for each stream, along with operating pressure. Identify the hot side and cold side clearly. If outlet temperatures are not fixed, state the process objective and available utility conditions so the design basis can be discussed.

3. Fluid properties and fouling behavior

Include fluid composition, phase, density, viscosity, specific heat and thermal conductivity when available. For mixtures, slurries or fluids whose properties change significantly with temperature, provide the best available composition and property data. Also describe solids content, scaling, fouling or polymerization risks, because these can affect heat-transfer surface, velocity and cleaning access.

4. Pressure drop, materials and design code

State the allowable pressure drop on each side, design pressure and design temperature, corrosion allowance and any special material requirements. Identify the project code and inspection requirements, such as ASME Section VIII, EN 13445 or a project-specific standard, where applicable. Materials and certification requirements should be confirmed for the actual service and destination.

5. Layout, maintenance and utilities

Confirm available installation space, nozzle orientation, connection sizes, lifting and maintenance clearances, and whether the unit needs removable bundles, covers or other cleaning access. Identify cooling water, steam, thermal oil or other utilities, including their supply conditions. For a package, clarify the interface with pumps, valves, instruments, piping and the control system.

What if some process data is unavailable?

Share the information already available and identify the unknowns. A vendor may prepare a preliminary review using explicit assumptions, but thermal performance, pressure drop and mechanical design must be confirmed using an agreed design basis before final approval.
